scholarship_name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) student scholarship - scheme-level baseline
scholarship_name_original: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM)
provider: European Commission / European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA)
applies_to_institution: any (EMJM consortium listed in the official EACEA catalogue)
applies_to_city: rotating - at least two study periods in two different countries
degree_level_covered: master (joint master, 60/90/120 ECTS)
amount_notes: 1400 EUR/month flat unit cost. Programme Guide: 'The scholarship is calculated as: 1 400 Euros/month x DS'. The scholarship 'shall cover travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs' - i.e. travel and installation are INSIDE the 1400/month, there is no separate travel or installation line under the 2021-2027 EMJM rules. Separately the consortium receives up to 750 EUR/month/student for institutional costs and 'projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory costs related to student participation in the course to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders' and 'cannot charge student application fees'. A 24-month EMJM scholarship is therefore worth 33600 EUR cash to the student plus a tuition waiver typically worth 9000-34000 EUR. NOTE: unlike the pre-2021 EMJMD there is NO higher Partner Country rate and NO separate 3000/4000 EUR travel top-up - do not quote legacy figures.
number_of_awards: max 50 regular scholarships per consortium over the whole grant (4+ editions), plus up to 18 extra NDICI scholarships and up to 3 IPA III scholarships for targeted regions; in practice most consortia award ~10-20 per intake
nationality_restrictions: Open to students of all nationalities worldwide. Consortium-level balance rule: 'no more than 10% of the total number of scholarships awarded during project implementation should be awarded to candidates from the same nationality' (does not apply to targeted-region top-ups). Students who already held an EMJM scholarship cannot get a second one.
tunisia_eligible_evidence: "Region 3 (Neighbourhood South): 18% of the budget available from NDICI. At least 20% of this amount should be allocated to Tunisia."
other_eligibility: Must hold a first-cycle higher education degree (or be in the final year of one) recognised as giving access to master studies; each consortium sets its own ECTS floor (usually 180 ECTS). No 12-month residence rule appears anywhere in the 2021-2027 EMJM section of the Erasmus+ Programme Guide - that rule belonged to the pre-2021 EMJMD Partner Country rate, which no longer exists. Compulsory physical mobility: two study periods in two different countries, both different from the student's country of residence at enrolment - a Tunisia-resident applicant satisfies this automatically.
application_window: Set by each consortium. Typical EMJM window for a September 2027 start: opens Oct-Nov 2026, closes Dec 2026 - Feb 2027. There is no central EU application - you apply to each consortium separately and the same form serves as the scholarship application.
deadline: Varies by consortium - see individual FEM rows
deadline_source_cycle: 2026-2027 Erasmus+ Programme Guide (funding rules); per-programme 2027 deadlines mostly not yet published as of 2026-08-22
apply_via: Directly to each EMJM consortium via its own online application portal
red_flags: The catalogue mixes projects selected 2017-2025; some listed programmes have exhausted their EU grant and no longer recruit (e.g. WAVES). Always confirm the consortium is still recruiting for the intake you want. Scholarship competition is severe - typically 1000+ applications for 10-20 funded places.
notes: SCHEME-LEVEL ROW - read this first, then the per-programme rows FEM-002 onward. Official EACEA catalogue holds 220 project entries / 212 distinct programmes as of 2026-08-22. THE HEADLINE FOR THIS CLIENT: Tunisia is not merely eligible, it is a named budget target - Region 3 (Neighbourhood South) takes 18% of the NDICI envelope and at least 20% of that is earmarked for Tunisia. Tunisian nationality is therefore an ADVANTAGE in EMJM selection, not a barrier. A 300-ECTS 5-year engineering diploma clears every EMJM entry bar (180 or 240 ECTS) with room to spare. Applies to paths A|C|N|G|H|R|J|L|AC|AD.
